question: At fixed source-file folds, does quantizing the shared seed affect pooled-model predictions, and how does final weight rounding change that effect?
scope: Paired deterministic computational ablation on reused TRAIN development data; not independent replicates or unseen-data causal efficacy.
folds: Exactly reuse five whole-file folds. Check each against original class-stratified SHA256(file) index modulo5; never move or split a file.
seed: First20 fit rows per class, in original order, eight original train() steps. Compute once/fold. Arms use that same float64 result or quantize(seed)/1024.
pooled_fit: Two fits/fold, each original120 full-batch steps, original class weighting, regularizer, learning rate and 257 fixed features. Identical fit rows and seed identities.
primary_endpoint: Total out-of-fold prediction disagreements FF vs QF across all1005 original TRAIN rows, isolating seed treatment before final weight quantization.
secondary_endpoints: FQ vs QQ seed-treatment disagreements after final quantization; FF vs FQ and QF vs QQ final-rounding disagreements; all full-population accuracies, confusion matrices and file-macro values; per-fold counts, shared-unit logits/margins, weight changes and clipping counts. Retain every outcome.
numerics: Unchanged np.argmax lowest-index ties. Float logits use raw integer feature x @ float weights. Integer logits are computed exactly in int64, then divided by1024 for comparable reported values; never divide feature x by8 for reporting.
controls: QF and QQ predictions must exactly reproduce the earlier retained float and integer OOF controls, respectively; fail otherwise. No calibration/evaluation/consumer task files may be loaded.
stop: Run the frozen five folds once; no hyperparameter selection, winning-arm adoption, data filtering or model publication. A nonzero effect establishes computational sensitivity only; zero disagreement does not prove zero logit/parameter perturbation.
